sections.summary: The House moved a Motion to reaffirm its commitment to a whole-of-nation approach to sustain trust by building an inclusive and safe digital society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Against this backdrop, we decided to move this Motion to reaffirm this House's commitment to adopt a whole-of-nation approach to sustain trust by building an inclusive and safe digital society.

sections.label: Safe online environment and trust
sections.summary: A safe online environment is crucial for building trust in a digital society because it influences confidence and willingness to engage in digital transactions and interactions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: On "safe", a safe online environment is crucial for building trust in a digital society because it directly influences people's confidence and willingness to engage in digital transactions and interactions.

sections.label: Combatting scams and fraud
sections.summary: Scams and fraudulent activities need to be combatted swiftly and effectively.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Second, we need to combat scams and fraudulent activities swiftly and effectively.

sections.label: Inclusivity builds digital trust
sections.summary: Inclusivity builds trust in a digital society by ensuring digitalisation's benefits are accessible to all, fostering fairness, equity and shared progress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Moving on to "inclusive", inclusivity builds trust in a digital society as it ensures that the benefits of digitalisation are accessible to all, fostering a sense of fairness, equity and shared progress.

sections.label: Safe inclusive digital society calls
sections.summary: The Communications and Information GPC and PAP MPs set out 13 calls to action for a whole-of-nation approach to a safer, more inclusive online space.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: To achieve a safe and inclusive digital society, everyone needs to play a part.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Hence, our GPC for Communications and Information, together with several People's Action Party (PAP) Members of Parliament (MPs), have set out 13 calls to action, urging a whole-of-nation approach to make the online space a safer and more inclusive one for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: First, Government to take the lead to set up information-sharing mechanism with the industry, modelled after "Stop Scams UK".

sections.label: Banks e-commerce authentication solutions
sections.summary: Banks and e-commerce platforms are called to adopt stronger authentication solutions like FIDO passkeys to keep accounts secure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Fourth, banks and e-commerce platforms to adopt stronger authentication solutions like the Fast Identity Online (FIDO) passkeys to keep our accounts secure.

sections.label: Social media harmful content accountability
sections.summary: Social media services are to be held accountable for the proliferation of harmful content and malicious ads.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Holding social media services accountable for the proliferation of harmful content and malicious ads.

sections.label: Age assurance and accessibility requirements
sections.summary: Social media and app distribution services are to step up age assurance, respond faster to harmful content reports, and essential service providers to ensure accessibility.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Requiring social media services and app distribution services to step up age assurance measures to better protect young users from harmful content.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Requiring social media services and app distribution services to improve timeliness in responding to user reports on harmful content on their platforms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Requiring essential service providers to ensure accessibility for all.

sections.label: PAP Motion 13 calls to action
sections.summary: PAP MPs proposed a Motion with 13 calls to action to reaffirm Parliament's commitment to an inclusive and safe digital society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In this context, I and the Members of Parliament from the PAP, have decided to propose this Motion, presenting 13 calls to action to reaffirm Parliament's commitment to build an inclusive and safe digital society through the combined efforts of the Government, businesses and the people to sustain trust. : As technology continues to develop, new methods of scams and cyber threats will also emerge.

sections.label: Scam calls blocked by telcos
sections.summary: IMDA revealed that of 1.6 billion international calls received yearly in Singapore, about 300 million suspected scam calls were blocked by telcos.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On scams and in particular scams through phone calls, Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) has revealed that out of the 1.6 billion international calls received in Singapore each year, about a quarter or 300 million were suspected to be scam calls and were blocked by telcos in the first nine months of last year.

sections.label: Local banks money lock
sections.summary: The three local banks offer money lock options that ringfence funds withdrawable only by physical visit to the bank.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On this, I note that the "money lock" options now offered by the three local banks are a practical feature to ringfence funds that can only be withdrawn by a physical visit to the bank.

sections.label: Seniors e-payments scam confidence
sections.summary: IMDA's report found 78% of seniors over 60 used e-payments online but only 44% were moderately confident identifying scams.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the IMDA's Singapore Digital Society Report last November, 78% of seniors over 60 used e-payments for online transactions but only 44% of the same group was moderately confident about identifying scams.

sections.label: RSD task force composition
sections.summary: The RSD task force's stated composition does not mention any representative from the MAS.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While the set-up of the RSD task force is an important development, I note that its stated composition does not mention any representative from the MAS.

sections.label: Deepfake videos Singapore rise

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to CNA, the prevalence of deepfake videos in Singapore jumped 500% in 2023 compared to the previous year.

sections.label: Petition pausing AI development
sections.summary: The institute's petition calling for a pause in AI development beyond GPT-4 gathered over 33,000 signatures, including AI company CEOs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In March this year, the institute launched a petition calling for a pause in AI development beyond GPT-4.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The petition gathered more than 33,000 signatures, including those of CEOs of AI companies.

sections.label: AI regulation capacity building
sections.summary: Effective AI regulation will require the Government to invest in constant capacity building.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To this end, having effective regulation for AI will require the Government to invest in constant capacity building.

sections.label: Consumer protection approach to scams
sections.summary: The Member calls on MAS and authorities to adopt a consumer protection approach to scams involving banking customers who lose savings online.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Even as Members on both sides of the House call for additional measures to scrutinise how banks treat their customers, I would like to once again call upon the MAS and the relevant authorities, to call upon and make the point I have raised previously in this House on multiple occasions, which is that there needs to be a consumer protection approach to scams involving banking customers who get scammed out of their savings online.

sections.label: Operating systems and online banking scams
sections.summary: A written answer showed one operating system accounted for virtually all online banking scams known to Police, while another did not figure much.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Yesterday, in a written question to the Minister for Communications and Information on operating systems, what was quite notable was that a certain operating system accounted for virtually all of the online banking scams made known to the Police, while a certain different operating system did not figure very much in the figures reported in that Parliamentary written answer.

sections.label: Banks, telcos and tech firm responsibility
sections.summary: The Member asks whether banks, telcos and tech firms shoulder enough responsibility compared with tangible goods providers in the physical world.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: If there is a home appliance in your kitchen and someone can trick you into pressing the wrong button so that someone is injured and loses their life savings along the way, you know what the approach will be when it comes to that home appliance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: I call upon this Government, MAS and the other agencies to take a hard look at the financial institutions and banks and ask: are the banks and telcos and technology firms shouldering enough responsibility in the digital world that tangible goods providers shoulder in the physical world?

sections.label: Deepfakes and democracy
sections.summary: The Member says deepfakes are a serious matter for democracies because if people cannot discern what is real, democracy cannot function.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The issue of deepfakes is going to be a serious matter for democracies around the world – because if we can no longer discern easily what is real and not real, you cannot even have a functioning democracy.

sections.label: Watermarking and proof of human
sections.summary: The Member calls on the Government to look at electronically watermarking content and proof of human to confirm content is real and human.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Therefore, as a society and as a government, we must not shy away from moving pre-emptively to address the issue of deepfakes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: I have called upon this Government to look at ways of electronically watermarking content, so called "proof of human", whether it is proof of human when someone transacts with an AI bot, with a tech firm online that may be giving answers by AI, but the broader point is that we need ways to confirm that the content is real and is a human.

sections.label: Whole-of-Government effort on technology
sections.summary: The Member says it is a whole-of-Government effort involving education, regulation, social norms and holding tech firms accountable.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: To sense, while at the same time not losing faith in society being able to move forward.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is of course, a whole-of-Government effort, there needs to be many ways to look at it, education, regulation, social norms, making sure tech firms are held accountable as well.

sections.label: AI investment in Government and industry
sections.summary: The speaker says investments in AI capability in Government and industry need to be doubled down.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: One last point I wanted to make is that we need to double down our investments in AI capability in our Government and in our industry as well.

sections.label: Betting on future AI capabilities
sections.summary: The speaker asks what investments could position Singapore as a world power in such capabilities in years ahead.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: What investments can we bet on that may seem tenuous today but which could put Singapore in a position to be a world power of such capabilities in years ahead.

sections.label: Internet access and emerging technology skills
sections.summary: The SGDS Report 2023 shows 99% household Internet access, but only 55% of those 18 and above and 24% of seniors know emerging technologies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: While it is encouraging to see in the Singapore Digital Society (SGDS) Report 2023 that 99% of households in Singapore have Internet access and there is a higher adoption of digital technology and skills even amongst seniors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: However, a study by IMDA showed that while Singaporeans are more willing to try new technologies, only 55% of those aged 18 and above and 24% of seniors know how to use devices and applications with emerging technologies such as voice recognition, virtual or augmented realities.

sections.label: Scams using sophisticated technologies
sections.summary: The passage states that with increasing use of sophisticated technologies and tools by scammers, persons affected and amounts lost to scams are significant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: With the increasing use of sophisticated technologies and tools by scammers, the number of persons affected by and amounts lost to scams is significant.

sections.label: Demands on Government and platform players
sections.summary: The passage says digital literacy alone is insufficient against digital risks, so more demands must be placed on Government, platform players, telcos and device manufacturers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Basically, what it means is that with the new technologies and sophisticated tools, user digital literacy will not be sufficient to safeguard against digital risks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: We must put more demands on Government, on platform players, telcos and device manufacturers to do more to improve the standards of security to enhance online safety of users on their platforms and for their services.

sections.label: Seniors owning smartphones
sections.summary: The passage states that the number of seniors owning smartphones has increased to 89% per the cited report.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The number of seniors owning smartphones has increased to 89%, as per the report I cited earlier.

sections.label: Digital adoption trust and confidence
sections.summary: The Singapore Digital Society Report 2023 found 55% of Singaporeans aged 15 and above accept technology risks, versus 33% of those aged 60 and older.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: As I have mentioned, it is key to building trust and confidence for digital adoption.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I just want to make another point that, the Singapore Digital Society (SGDS) Report 2023 did say that 55% of Singaporeans aged 15 and above are willing to accept the risks that come with the use of technology and only 33% amongst those aged 60 and older.

sections.label: Singapore second National AI Strategy
sections.summary: NAIS 2.0, launched last December by Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, outlines AI opportunities, risks, and commitment to a trusted and responsible AI ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: An example is Singapore's second National AI Strategy (NAIS 2.0), which was recently launched last December by Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: It outlines both the opportunities and risks of AI.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: It outlines also our ambition and commitment to building a trusted and responsible AI ecosystem, driving innovation and growth through AI and empowering our people and businesses to understand and engage with AI.

sections.label: Diverse workforce and senior workers
sections.summary: A diverse workforce lets organisations use different perspectives, skills and experiences, and employers must tap senior workers' wealth and experience.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: A diverse workforce will enable organisations to leverage different perspectives, skills and experiences because you need that to develop new ideas to grow and thrive in a digital society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: On that note, I do want to make a point to employers and organisations that we must tap on the vast pool of wealth and experience of senior workers and bring that into that diverse workforce to enable us to find new ways, both young and old, to create new ways of doing things with technology.

sections.label: Inclusive and safe digital society
sections.summary: An inclusive and safe digital society aims for everyone to participate and benefit with no one left behind, requiring all to do their part.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: All these are necessary, but the purpose of an inclusive and safe digital society is to ensure that everyone can actively participate and benefit to make their lives better and that no one is left behind.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: But in order to achieve this, it will take all of us to do our part to enable an inclusive, trusted and safe digital society.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While I support the Motion as it stands, I will elaborate in my speech today on why, as currently conceived, it remains fundamentally unfair in stark contrast to its stated aim of equitable sharing.

sections.label: 50/50 split bargaining solution
sections.summary: Many have concluded that a 50/50 split or something close to it is the only just solution to most bargaining situations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While there are variations, many have concluded that a 50/50 split or something close to it, is the only just solution to most bargaining situations.

sections.label: Laws limiting fraudulent transaction liability
sections.summary: At the simplest level, these could be laws that limit liability on fraudulent transactions to a pre-specified amount.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: At the simplest level, these could be laws that limit liability on fraudulent transactions to a pre-specified amount.

sections.label: Waterfall approach for losses
sections.summary: The framework proposes a waterfall approach where financial institutions and telecom operators bear full losses only if they fail their prescribed duties.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Perhaps more importantly, what the framework proposes is to adopt a "waterfall approach", where financial institutions and telecom operators will only bear the full losses when they "fail to discharge their respective prescribed duties" and will not require payouts to be made to consumers if they are deemed to have done so.

sections.label: Consumer co-payments for fraud
sections.summary: Requiring savers to absorb a reasonable loss, such as $100 or $500, aligns consumer incentives with combating fraud.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Furthermore, just as we co-payments in most insurance plans, so long as savers are required to absorb at least some reasonable amount of loss – say, an upper limit of $100 or $500 – then it is hard to claim that the consumer incentives are not well-aligned with combating fraud.

sections.label: CPF fraud insurance scheme reversal
sections.summary: Minister Tan See Leng suggested openness to such mechanisms, but the Ministry said it had no intention to consider insurance schemes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In his initial discussion of CPF-related fraud, Minister Tan See Leng suggested an openness through such mechanisms.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, this was walked back the very next day with the Ministry stating that it had and I quote, "no intention" to consider insurance schemes.

sections.label: Removing clickable links insufficient
sections.summary: Removing clickable links in emails or SMSes was rolled out in January 2022, but these measures alone remain insufficient to stem financial fraud.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Another is to remove clickable links in emails or SMSes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But it is noteworthy that while these were first rolled out in January 2022 and if the continued proliferation of scams over the past two years are any guide, these measures alone remain insufficient to stem the tide of financial fraud.

sections.label: Cooling-off periods limited effectiveness
sections.summary: Cooling-off periods work only if victims know or accept they were scammed, and even professionals may succumb, per a 2018 study.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Similarly, cooling-off periods only work to the extent that victims are even aware or accept that they have been scammed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Unless we think that we surely will never fall victim to such schemes, recall that many fraudsters are extremely skilled confidence artists and even professionals may succumb, as a study by the Police Psychological Services Division conducted in 2018 has shown.

sections.label: Loss absorption to rebuild trust
sections.summary: Regulators should require loss absorption by financial institutions and communications companies with consumer liability capped at $100 or $500.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To rebuild trust, regulators should require actual loss absorption by financial institutions and communications companies with an upper limit to consumer liability of $100 or $500 when losses are perhaps inevitably and unfortunately realised.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This will not only be fair but help evolve the system in the long run to a more robust one.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Thousands of non-consensual sexually explicit photos and videos of women and schoolgirls were distributed to more than 44,000 members.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: About a month ago, a 65-year-old Singaporean retiree lost her life savings in 15 days.

sections.label: IMDA online safety code
sections.summary: IMDA's Code of Practice took effect in July 2023, requiring designated social media services to curb sexual, violent and self-harm content.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In July 2023, IMDA's Code of Practice online safety came into effect, requiring designated social media services to enhance online safety in Singapore and curb the spread of sexual content, violent content, suicide and self-harm content on their platforms.

sections.label: Wife-sharing forum case
sections.summary: Seven men met on an online forum from 2010, discussed wife-sharing fantasies, acted on them and live streamed the acts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: A few months ago, we were shaken by the disturbing news of seven men meeting on an online forum as early as in 2010, before discussing their wife-sharing fantasies and turning their plans into action, even live streaming these acts.

sections.label: Surf Safe Initiative students
sections.summary: The Surf Safe Initiative, launched in 2022, cultivates safer cyber habits among secondary students and has reached 33,944 of them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Surf Safe Initiative was launched in 2022 to cultivate safer cyber habits among secondary students and to date has reached 33,944 of them.

sections.label: Digital Enablement Programme question
sections.summary: The passage asks how many individuals the Digital Enablement Programme has served since its inception.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: How many individuals has the Digital Enablement Programme served since its inception?

sections.label: YouTube Priority Flagger programme
sections.summary: In July 2023 Google launched the YouTube Priority Flagger programme, training community partners to flag violating content directly to Google for prioritised review.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In July 2023, Google launched the YouTube Priority Flagger programme, which empowers community partners by training them to assess content that violates YouTube community guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These priority flaggers include organisations such as Touch and SG Her Empowerment, who are able to flag content directly to Google, allowing problematic content to be prioritised for review.

sections.label: Online harms study and strategy
sections.summary: An SG Her Empowerment study found three in five Singaporeans experienced online harms, and the passage calls for awareness, support and an agile national digital strategy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: According to a study conducted by SG Her Empowerment (SHE), three in five Singaporeans have experienced online harms, or know someone who experienced it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Many such cases have been reported, one of which involved a lewd survey on local female asatizah in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Communicating judiciously, as well as having better awareness and support for victims of online harms, will certainly have a big impact as we try to create a safe online space for all segments of society. : Sir, every technological advancement comes with its risks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To this end, I hope that as a country, we continue to pursue a national digital strategy that is agile and collaborative in approach as well as inclusive, empowering and human-centered.

sections.label: Rising digital fraud attacks
sections.summary: Singapore received 32 million digital fraud attacks last year, and scam and cyber crime cases rose almost 70% in the first half of 2023.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Digital fraud attacks are on the rise, with Singapore receiving 32 million such attacks last year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to Singapore Police Force data, in the first half of 2023, there were close to 25,000 scam and cyber crime cases, an increase of almost 70% from the same period in 2022.

sections.label: Online harassment survey findings
sections.summary: An SG Her Empowerment survey found 52% of respondents reporting online harassment were aged 15 to 24, and two in five victims reported severe consequences.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In a recent survey conducted by SG Her Empowerment, a local independent non-profit organisation, 52% of respondents who reported a personal experience of online harassment or discrimination were between 15 and 24 years of age.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the same survey, two in five victims reported experiencing at least one severe consequence as a result of the harassment or discrimination, including physical and mental health issues and suicidal ideation.

sections.label: Incentives for responsible online behaviour
sections.summary: The passage proposes incentives for responsible online behaviour and describes digital citizenship as acting responsibly online by adhering to the law and protecting privacy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One way to move forward is to consider introducing incentives for responsible online behavior, whether through recognition programmes or other tangible rewards.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Digital citizenship requires individuals to act responsibly online by adhering to the law, protecting privacy, managing reputation and considering how one's online behaviour impacts on oneself, acquaintances and the broader digital community.

sections.label: Promoting digital citizenship values
sections.summary: Promoting digital citizenship values of empathy, tolerance and inclusivity, and increasing digital trust and literacy, can lay the foundation for everyone to engage and thrive digitally.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Promoting digital citizenship values, emphasising empathy, tolerance and inclusivity will foster a positive online culture and ensure a safe and more harmonious digital society.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By increasing digital trust, advancing digital literacy and nurturing a culture of digital citizenship, we can lay the foundation for a future where everyone all can engage and thrive in the digital world.

sections.label: Woodgrove resident's impersonation scam loss
sections.summary: A Woodgrove resident in his late 60s lost close to $800,000 of his and his wife's life savings due to an impersonation scam.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: A sobering example comes from one of my Woodgrove residents in his late 60s, who had lost close to $800,000 of his and his wife's life savings due to an impersonation scam.

sections.label: Mr Yu's malware booking scam
sections.summary: Mr Yu entered his OTP on a bogus website while booking a hotel online, and the bank later said he is expected to bear 50% of over $6,000 in unauthorised transactions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Back then, Mr Yu was making an online hotel booking when he fell prey to a malware by entering his OTP on a bogus website.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: He promptly contacted the bank's customer service upon discovering several unauthorised transactions amounting to over $6,000 charged to his credit card.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Almost six months later, the bank replied after completing their investigations to inform him that he is expected to bear 50% of the unauthorised transacted sum.

sections.label: Banks blaming customers for scams
sections.summary: The speaker disagrees with banks that expect individual customers to fend for themselves against scams.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, in a recent news article where another bank was interviewed after one of its customers lost his entire life savings due to another malware scam, the bank likewise took a similar position that their customers "remain the singular most effective defence and strongly urged them to exercise vigilance and caution in this ever-evolving threat landscape." I disagree with the position taken by the banks in both cases, in that they conveniently expected their individual customers to fend for themselves.

sections.label: OCBC Money Lock and scam insurance
sections.summary: The speaker hopes MAS mandates OCBC Money Lock across all banks and considers a scam insurance scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In November last year, OCBC introduced its anti-scam security feature called OCBC Money Lock, which allows customers to lock away funds in their bank accounts and can only be unlocked after the customer's identity has been verified by the bank.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This is a good initiative which I hope MAS can mandate to be rolled out across all of the banks in Singapore and to encourage sign-ups by our seniors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In addition, MAS can also consider working with banks and insurance companies to introduce an insurance scheme akin to the concept of Deposit Insurance Scheme, which anyone with a bank account can purchase to protect their monies in the event that they fall prey to an online scam.

sections.label: Global annual scam losses
sections.summary: The Straits Times reported global annual losses due to scams of $1.4 trillion in October last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In October last year, The Straits Times reported that globally, the annual loss due to scams is a staggering $1.4 trillion.

sections.label: Shared Responsibility Framework duties and payouts
sections.summary: The Shared Responsibility Framework assigns duties to financial institutions and telcos and requires payouts where duties are breached.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The proposed Shared Responsibility Framework (SRF), which assigns financial institutions and telcos relevant duties to mitigate phishing scams and requires payouts to affected scam victims where these duties are breached, is a step in the right direction, but it is just a baby step.

sections.label: UK full reimbursement and co-sharing
sections.summary: The speaker notes UK-style full reimbursement and suggests co-sharing liabilities between bank and consumer.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In contrast to Singapore's framework, jurisdictions like the UK have moved towards mandating full reimbursement to scam victims by banks, except in cases of fraud or gross negligence by the consumer.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This model has also been considered in Australia and the European Union (EU).

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I acknowledge that there are moral hazard issues with a full reimbursement and would thus like to suggest a co-sharing of liabilities between the bank and the consumer.

sections.label: Banking app versions with reimbursement
sections.summary: Banks can offer a maximum-security, low-convenience app version with 75% reimbursement for scams not covered by the SRF.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Banks can offer different versions of banking apps and processes; for example, one with maximum security features and low convenience, and it comes with a 75% reimbursement of financial losses by the banks in cases of online scams not covered by the SRF.

sections.label: Reimbursement loss upper limit
sections.summary: Reimbursements can be subject to an upper limit of a loss amount equal to the basic retirement sum.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Reimbursements can be subject to an upper limit of a loss amount equivalent to the basic retirement sum.

sections.label: CPF online withdrawal limit
sections.summary: From 30 November 2023, a default online CPF withdrawal limit of $2,000 a day applies to members aged 55 and above, adjustable up to $200,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In October 2023, my colleague Mr Leong Mun Wai asked a Parliamentary Question regarding why the CPF website has not implemented security measures commonly implemented by the banks, such as transaction limits and kill switches.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It is heartening to know that with effect from 30 November 2023, a default online CPF withdrawal limit of $2,000 a day will be applied to all CPF members aged 55 and above.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, this default daily limit can still be adjusted to any amount up to $200,000 at any time online.

sections.label: Bank bears fraud losses
sections.summary: Consumers may choose a banking application with high security features, and in the event of fraud losses the bank must bear 75%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For example, consumers can choose to use a banking application with high security features, which may inconvenience them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But in the event of fraud losses, the bank must bear 75% of the losses.

sections.label: Scam victims' losses and trauma
sections.summary: Victims suffer mental and emotional trauma and financial implications for family members, and society picks up the tab; a study found Singapore had the highest amount lost to scams per victim.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Beyond financial losses, victims also suffer from mental and emotional trauma, such as the embarrassment of having fallen for a scam.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: There are also financial implications on their family members, such as a child who may by law be responsible for the maintenance of a parent who has lost their life savings to a scammer.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Society must ultimately pick up the tab when people lose their life savings to scammers and the ability to live independently and must instead rely on handouts and charity to survive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: A recent study by the Global Anti-Scam Alliance revealed that Singapore has the dubious honour of being the country with the highest amount lost to scams per victim.

sections.label: Seniors fear scams, Singpass passwords
sections.summary: In engagements with Woodland seniors for Healthier SG, some ignored MOH messages fearing scams, and most relied on less secure password authentication on Singpass.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: More recently, in my engagements with Woodland seniors to encourage them to sign up for Healthier SG, I found a not insignificant number of seniors were ignoring the messages from the Ministry of Health (MOH) as they were afraid of scams.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I also saw that most of them were reliant on less secure password authentication on their Singpass app, partly because they did not know how to use and partly because they did not trust biometric authentication.

sections.label: AI deepfakes online trust
sections.summary: Fake news and images are not new, but the proliferation of deepfakes used in harmful ways such as investment scams shows AI presents a new frontier in online trust and safety.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Fake news, fake images – they are not new in online trust and safety.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But as we move from fun face swapping apps and camera filters to the rapid proliferation of deepfakes being used in harmful ways, such as investment scams featuring our own Prime Minister, it is clear that AI presents a new frontier in online trust and safety.

sections.label: Online safety and scam safeguards
sections.summary: Passage calls for stronger safeguards holding social media services accountable for harmful content, scams and malicious ads, citing the Online Safety Act, Online Safety Code and Shared Responsibility Framework.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: First, increase safeguards and hold social media services accountable for the proliferation of harmful content, scams and malicious ads, including AI-generated content, to protect consumers, especially children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The passing of the Online Safety Act in February 2023 and the subsequent release of the Online Safety Code by IMDA in July 2023 have strengthened the regulatory framework, holding social media services accountable to take preventive measures against online harm.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Government has also rolled out a series of measures to protect against online scams, including the much discussed Shared Responsibility Framework slated to be implemented this year.

sections.label: AI deepfake law coverage
sections.summary: Passage states that online harms from AI-generated content such as deepfakes may not be sufficiently covered by current laws.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Online harms related to AI-generated content such as deepfakes may not be sufficiently covered by current laws.

sections.label: UK deepfake pornography law
sections.summary: Passage says the UK Online Safety Act made transmitting deepfake pornography illegal and requires platforms to quickly remove it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Looking around, the UK Online Safety Act has made transmitting deepfake pornography illegal and platforms will need to quickly act to remove them from their platforms.

sections.label: Government AI deployment push
sections.summary: Passage urges Government to deploy high value AI use cases at scale in public services and advance online trust and safety research, citing the National AI Strategy 2.0.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Third, Government to lead the way by deploying AI at scale through high value use cases in public services and advancing research into online trust and safety.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The recently launched National AI Strategy 2.0, which I am hopeful will get a good airing in Parliament in due course articulates a vision for "AI for the Public Good, for Singapore and the World".

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Among other actions, the Government seeks to pursue meaningful use cases in both public services and industry that will deliver outsized impact to our lives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to make a big push to deploy high value use cases, at scale, in public services.

sections.label: AI governance participation update
sections.summary: Passage asks the Minister for an update on Singapore's participation in the AI governance and safety space.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide an update on our participation in the AI governance and safety space?

sections.label: CPF withdrawal safeguards at 55
sections.summary: Passage states that at 55 only amounts above the Basic Retirement Sum can be withdrawn from the CPF Ordinary or Special Account, and CPF safeguards are no less stringent than banks'.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The way we have constructed the CPF, is, at 55, you have the Basic Retirement Sum within the Retirement Account.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: So, only amounts above the Basic Retirement Sum can be withdrawn from the CPF Ordinary Account or Special Account.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Our CPF safeguards are no less stringent than what banks have put in place.

sections.label: Singpass facial verification losses
sections.summary: After Singpass facial verification began in June 2023, no unauthorised losses were observed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Member may also take comfort in knowing that after the Singpass facial verification implementation in June 2023, no unauthorised losses was observed.

sections.label: Banks and physical tokens
sections.summary: With 87 scams daily, banks should carry more responsibility and reintroduce physical tokens as default multi-factor authentication.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Given that an average of 87 scams are taking place every day in Singapore, each day of delay will be one day too late for many scam victims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Banks must shoulder a greater responsibility in protecting their customers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I echo Ms Sylvia Lim's earlier call for banks to reintroduce physical tokens as a default measure for multi-factor authentication for all their customers.

sections.label: MAS measures versus scam cases
sections.summary: MAS imposes punitive measures for online banking and ATM downtimes, but this rigour is absent in scam cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On one hand, MAS imposes very punitive measures like restrictions on acquisitions and additional capital requirements on banks when there are brief downtimes in online banking and ATM services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On the other hand, this level of decisiveness and rigour is markedly absent in addressing scam cases.

sections.label: Handset side loading security
sections.summary: Handsets sold in Singapore should disable side loading by default, as about 37% of residents do not regularly update devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: All handsets sold in Singapore should be required to disable side loading of apps by default and make it difficult for end users to override critical security features.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: MCI has revealed that a notable proportion of residents, approximately 37%, do not regularly update their devices.

sections.label: Banks consumer protection responsibility
sections.summary: Banks must significantly increase their responsibility towards consumer protection, including by providing physical tokens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, banks must significantly increase their responsibility towards consumer protection, including by providing physical tokens to customers.

sections.label: Tech accountability and anti-scam agency
sections.summary: The Government should hold technology companies more accountable, and a central anti-scam agency should oversee anti-scam efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Fourth, the Government needs to hold technology companies more accountable for their security of their platforms and devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And finally, a central anti-scam agency should oversee and be ultimately accountable for the Government's anti-scam efforts.

sections.label: Friedman on business social responsibility
sections.summary: Milton Friedman argued in 1970 that business's social responsibility is to increase its profits, shaping corporate growth since.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 1970, economist Milton Friedman asked a fundamental question, "What is the role of business in society?" In response, he submitted an argument to the New York Times stating that, "The social responsibility of business is to increase its profits." Since then, this narrative has shaped the growth of corporations.

sections.label: Regulators educating companies on user rights
sections.summary: The speaker suggests regulators proactively educate companies on respecting user rights to address unsolicited marketing and user powerlessness over data.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To address the harmful effects of unsolicited marketing and the powerlessness that users experience in relation to the data that we hand over to the companies, I would suggest that regulators take a proactive approach to educate companies on respect for user rights.

sections.label: Updated social responsibilities in digital age
sections.summary: The speaker urges punitive action, guardrails, forward-looking companies, worker training, and united workers and users to set updated digital-age standards.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Regulators should consider imposing punitive action on recalcitrant companies and establish guardrails to keep in check companies exhibiting such predatory behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To address the precarity of workers in the face of technological innovation and disruptions, I would urge companies to adopt a forward-looking approach.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, a socially responsible company would work together with unions and agencies on continual training and on-the-job learning for their workforce to improve workforce mobility across technologies.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Just as Friedman's narrative was reshaped by the rise of social consciousness in society, the responsibility is upon us as workers and users to make a difference.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would encourage workers and users to unite under representative bodies, such as the unions and associations and to put forth our updated expectations on the social responsibilities of businesses in the digital age.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By working closely with Government and like-minded businesses and organisations and leveraging the tripartite framework, we can establish updated standards and legitimise the norms to form the bedrock for a safe and inclusive digital society.

sections.label: Cyberbullying risk among Singapore children
sections.summary: Studies show four in 10 children aged eight to 12 in Singapore risk cyberbullying, with a Sunlight AfA survey finding similar youth experiences.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In Singapore, this issue is particularly concerning, as studies show that four in 10 children aged eight to 12 are at risk of cyberbullying, a risk that increases for teenagers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Reinforcing these findings, an online survey by the Sunlight Alliance for Action (AfA) revealed that a similar proportion of youths experience cyberbullying, leading to deep emotional scars.

sections.label: Code of Practice and age assurance gap
sections.summary: The speaker applauds MCI's Code of Practice for Online Safety but notes a gap in accurately determining users' ages beyond self-declaration.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Policies and regulations must be robust, holding social media services and application developers accountable.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Therefore, I applaud MCI for the Code of Practice for Online Safety, which is crucial in governing digital content and interactions to create a safer online environment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Code mandates social media services like Meta and Google, which have significant reach in Singapore, to establish systems and processes to shield users, especially children, from online harm.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: However, while social media services and application developers have policies specifically for young users, a critical gap remains, the challenge of accurately determining the age of users.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Beyond self-declaration, these platforms need reliable age assurance measures, as the current system is easily circumvented.

sections.label: IMDA initiative for online safety
sections.summary: The speaker says IMDA's latest initiative, including the Code of Practice for Online Security, is an important step to improve online safety for children.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The latest initiative by IMDA, including the Code of Practice for Online Security, is an important step to improve online safety, especially for children.

sections.label: Rise in scam incidences
sections.summary: Scam incidences rose fivefold between 2018 and 2022, and 2023 losses will likely exceed half a billion dollars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Between 2018 to 2022, scam incidences have been reported to increase fivefold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Losses to scams in 2023 will likely again cost us more than half a billion dollars.

sections.label: Digital banking security measures
sections.summary: In January 2022, MAS and ABS announced measures, including banks removing clickable links in emails or SMSes to customers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In January 2022, MAS and the Association of Banks in Singapore (ABS) announced additional measures to bolster the security of digital banking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Among these measures, banks in Singapore have removed clickable links in emails or SMSes sent to customers.

sections.label: Government website accessibility rate
sections.summary: The Enabling Masterplan 2030 report states about 61% of all high traffic Government websites are accessible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to the Enabling Masterplan 2030 report, about 61% of all high traffic Government websites are accessible.

sections.label: Singapore Digital Service Standard scope
sections.summary: Singapore's DSS aligns with WCAG 2.1 AA, applies only to Government agencies, and no legislation requires company accessibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In Singapore, our Digital Service Standard (DSS) aligns with WCAG 2.1 at the AA level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The DSS framework in Singapore applies exclusively to Government agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We do not have legislation in Singapore that requires companies to make their products and services accessible to persons with disabilities.

sections.label: Human verification on e-commerce sites
sections.summary: Some e-commerce websites use puzzles or sliders to verify that users are human.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For instance, some e-commerce websites use puzzles or sliders to verify that users are, indeed, human.

sections.label: EU accessibility directive example
sections.summary: The 2019 EU Directive sets accessibility standards for consumer banking and e-commerce services, among others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: An example is the 2019 EU Directive, which sets accessibility standards for consumer banking and e-commerce services, among others.

sections.label: Digital accessibility proposals
sections.summary: Proposals to require essential online platforms to meet accessibility frameworks, expand PSG support, and train future web designers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, could we consider requiring non-Government, essential services, starting with high traffic online platforms to conform with an accessibility framework similar to DSS?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, to encourage smaller businesses, could the Government consider expanding the scope of the Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG) to support the development and improvement of websites, mobile applications, digital products and services and make them accessible to all?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Third, could the Government work with Institutes of Higher Learning to ensure that future web designers and programmers are sufficiently trained on digital accessibility?

sections.label: Nasi lemak couple scam
sections.summary: A scammer's app took the life savings of a couple who ran a nasi lemak store.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Years of working at their nasi lemak store, saw their five children through school, only for their dreams of retirement to vanish in a single tap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: A scammer's cunning app devoured their life savings, leaving them helpless and heartbroken.

sections.label: Seniors digital skills update
sections.summary: Asks for an update on how many seniors the SG Digital Office has reached and how many more need reaching.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Over the years, the SG Digital Office (SDO) have done much to equip seniors with necessary digital skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I wish to ask for an update on how many seniors have been reached and how many more do we need to reach?

sections.label: Centralised scam support agency
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government can consider a centralized agency managing scam support networks and helplines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To address the prevalence of online scams, can the Government consider a centralized agency managing these support networks and helplines?

sections.label: Scam money retrieval timelines
sections.summary: States retrieval of money from perpetrators is difficult and notes prior advocacy for timelines to update residents, especially seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, once perpetrators acquire money, retrieval is understandably difficult.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I have previously advocated in this House for timelines for law enforcement agencies to update residents on such matters, especially seniors impacted by online scams.

sections.label: Cyber resilience and scam comparison
sections.summary: Asks for plans to strengthen cyber resilience and infrastructure and how Singapore's financial scam fight compares to other cities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share some of the plans to further strengthen cyber resilience and infrastructure?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: On this note, I wish to ask how does our fight against financial scams compare to other cities like Hong Kong, New York and London?

sections.label: Citizens aged 65 and above
sections.summary: The Population In Brief report says citizens aged 65 and above are about 19%, expected to reach around 24% by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to the annual Population In Brief report, Singapore citizens aged 65 and above make up around 19% of our demographic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That figure is expected to increase and by 2030, around 24% of our citizens will be aged 65 and above.

sections.label: Banks removing physical cheques
sections.summary: Banks cite cost factors for removing physical cheques or charging for their use despite record profits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In spite of posting record profits, banks continue to cite cost factors as the reason why they have decided to do away with physical cheques or to implement charges for their use – never mind that this is a mode of payment that generations of Singaporeans have been used to.

sections.label: National Gallery People's Gallery project
sections.summary: In 2021, the National Gallery Singapore launched a project called The People's Gallery.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2021, the National Gallery Singapore launched a superb project called The People's Gallery.

sections.label: Mind Palace virtual transport for residents
sections.summary: Eugene and his team at Mind Palace virtually transport nursing home residents to familiar places such as old homes, neighbourhoods, Haw Par Villa and Chinatown.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In his Mind Palace social enterprise, Eugene and his team are able to virtually transport nursing home residents to evocative places which are familiar to them, such as their old homes or neighbourhoods or even places of interest such as Haw Par Villa and Chinatown.

sections.label: Mind Palace trials and immersive rooms
sections.summary: Mind Palace has conducted hundreds of trials and built five permanent immersive rooms at various eldercare facilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To date, Mind Palace has conducted hundreds of trials and built five permanent immersive rooms at various eldercare facilities.

sections.label: HSBC Hong Kong fraud prevention exhibition
sections.summary: HSBC Bank in Hong Kong held an art exhibition last November to promote public awareness on fraud prevention and online scams.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The final example I would like to refer to is that of HSBC Bank in Hong Kong, which last November, organised an art exhibition aimed at promoting public awareness on fraud prevention and online scams.

sections.label: Digital literacy for seniors
sections.summary: The passage notes a step to raise awareness among digital natives and mentions DBS Foundation and POSB engaging getai performers to educate seniors on digital literacy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is indeed a good step in the right direction to raise awareness amongst digital natives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But I also read with interest earlier this week that the DBS Foundation and POSB have engaged with getai performers to entertain and educate seniors on digital literacy.

sections.label: Trust and unity surveys
sections.summary: The passage states that a 2023 Edelman Trust study found the Government most trusted, and a 2022 Pew Research found 75% of Singaporeans felt more united after COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Based on a study by the Edelman Trust in 2023, our Government remains the most trusted institution in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In a 2022 Pew Research, 75% of Singaporeans polled shared that they felt more united after COVID-19, topping the list of 13 countries.

sections.label: Household digital access rates
sections.summary: The passage states the Singapore Digital Society Report shows 99% internet connectivity for all households and 98% of households with school-going children have computer access, citing Pasir Ris East laptop distribution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The latest Singapore Digital Society Report indicates that through schemes such as DigitalAccess@Home and NEU PC, Singapore has a 99% internet connectivity rate for all households and 98% of households with school-going children have access to computers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: An example is in Pasir Ris East, where we worked with Schneider Electric to distribute 100 laptops to children from lower-income families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, what I find surprising is that, despite all these programmes only 98% of household with school-going kids have access to computers.

sections.label: Essential digital skills curriculum
sections.summary: The passage asks whether essential digital skills such as basic coding, robotics, applied AI, cybersecurity and digital wellness can be included as core curriculum in primary and secondary schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Can we identify essential digitals skills such as basic coding, robotics, applied AI, cybersecurity and digital wellness to be included as core curriculum in primary and secondary schools, so that all our students have access and are exposed to these essential digital skills at an early age?

sections.label: Non-examinable digital curriculum proposal
sections.summary: The passage proposes including these topics in the core curriculum as non-examinable and replacing topics that may not be as critical in the future economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: To ease the academic load on our students, I propose that these topics are included into the core curriculum as non-examinable, while we replace topics that may not be as critical in the future economy.

sections.label: Financial institutions and scam consequences
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the approach can be reviewed so financial institutions bear some consequences for scams by unauthorised transactions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Can we review the approach such that financial institutions bear some consequences for scams by unauthorised transactions?

sections.label: Freezing bank accounts review
sections.summary: A question asks whether the process of freezing bank accounts can be reviewed for the entire investigation period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Can we review the process of freezing bank accounts for the entire duration of the investigation period?

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to the most recent National Business Survey 2022/2023 by the Singapore Business Federation (SBF), 64% of businesses expressed concern over the high costs associated with adopting new technologies.

sections.label: SMEs prioritising cyber resilience
sections.summary: A 2023 SCCCI survey found 32% of SMEs prioritising resilience against cyber threats, up from 11% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Furthermore, a 2023 survey conducted by the Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCCI) revealed that 32% of small and medium enterprises (SMEs) are prioritising the strengthening of their resilience against cyber threats, marking a significant increase from 11% in 2022, indicating a growing awareness and commitment to cybersecurity in the SME sector.

sections.label: SME co-funding for cybersecurity
sections.summary: Eligible SMEs can use up to 70% co-funding under this scheme to make advanced cybersecurity more accessible and affordable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To encourage participation and alleviate financial burdens, eligible SMEs can avail themselves of up to 70% co-funding under this scheme, making advanced cybersecurity more accessible and affordable.

sections.label: Tiered support for digitalisation
sections.summary: Suggests tiered grants for advanced AI and blockchain adoption, support for overseas digital projects, and a dedicated SME assistance channel for cybersecurity and AI governance breaches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For instance, a tiered support approach with a higher grant support quantum for the adoption of advanced AI and blockchain technology may be necessary to help companies to progress along their digitalisation roadmap beyond basic process and operational automation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There is also scope to consider expanding existing schemes to support digital projects where development work is conducted outside of Singapore for operational and cost efficiency, given the tight IT manpower pool here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Additionally, establishing a dedicated assistance channel for SMEs to reach out when addressing potential cybersecurity or AI governance breaches would provide a safety net, ensuring that SMEs have the support they need when they need it.

sections.label: Upskilling grants and data ethics
sections.summary: Proposes a grant scheme for employee upskilling and new technologies, a centralised SME platform, and ethical data practices ensuring privacy, consent and transparency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To assist companies to continue their commitment to upskilling their workers, as proposed in the SBF-KPMG budget recommendations, the Government can also consider complementing the efforts of businesses by introducing a grant scheme to support costs related to employee upskilling and adoption of new technologies such as AI and machine learning, as well as by providing a secure and convenient centralised platform for SMEs to access these upskilling services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As custodians of customer data, we must adhere to the highest standards of ethics, ensuring that every piece of information is collected, stored, and used with the utmost respect for privacy and consent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This means being transparent about our data practices, providing customers with clear choices, and taking proactive steps to protect their information from breaches and misuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By committing to these ethical practices, we not only comply with regulations but also fortify our reputation, foster customer loyalty, and contribute to a more trustworthy digital ecosystem.

sections.label: Hawkers and Seniors Go Digital
sections.summary: Cites IMDA's Hawkers go Digital, which subsidised hawkers to go online, and Seniors Go Digital, which trains seniors at heartland locations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For example, Hawkers go Digital, an initiative by the IMDA to subsidise hawkers to move their business online and accept digital platforms, was rolled out, bringing many heartland hawkers into the digital world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Seniors Go Digital, likewise, is targeted at seniors with courses available at locations throughout the heartlands and trains them in the range of functions and services they are able to access through their phones.

sections.label: Scam perpetrators located overseas

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Singapore Police is closely plugged in with Interpol and counterparts in other agencies, but it is sometimes difficult to trace exactly where each of the numerous scams originate from.

sections.label: Woman lost over $1 million

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: By the time she approached me, she had spent more than $1 million dollars.

sections.label: Three-pronged anti-scam approach
sections.summary: Describes Singapore's three-pronged approach to fight scams and SPF downstream measures, including a crackdown averting over $12.6 million in losses and OCBC robotic process automation work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Balancing these considerations, Singapore has taken a three-pronged approach to fight scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Second, the Singapore Police Force (SPF) adopts downstream measures, including trying to chase down scams syndicates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I think there was a report in The Straits Times that at least one scam had been successfully cracked with this, adverting over $12.6 million in losses – a drop in the ocean but a step in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: One example of this the work with OCBC Bank in March 2023 to use robotic processes automation to allow them to identify potential scammers.

sections.label: Private-sector-led scam reimbursement initiative
sections.summary: This private-sector-led initiative may have been partly motivated by UK legal measures requiring banks to reimburse APP scam victims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: What is interesting here is this is a private-sector-led initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This may have been partly motivated by UK's legal measures to require banks to reimburse victims of authorised push payment or APP scams.

sections.label: UK fraud reduction aim
sections.summary: It is uncertain whether this will work or increase moral hazard and frauds, though the UK aims to reduce fraud by 10%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The jury is now whether this will work or whether it may increase moral hazard and increase the incidence of frauds, but we should keep a watch on it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It should be noted that despite the seemingly radical approach, the UK's aim is to reduce fraud by 10%.

sections.label: MAS risk-sharing framework review
sections.summary: MAS' risk-sharing framework is a start and can be reviewed and modified to balance risk allocation among players.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: MAS' risk-sharing framework is a start and it is one thing that can be reviewed and modified, if needed, to balance the allocation of risks amongst the different players.

sections.label: Digital inclusion and security
sections.summary: Avoiding digitisation is not an option, so inclusion and security must be addressed, with Minister Josephine Teo speaking on digital trust and safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I do not think avoiding digitisation is an option.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: However, in riding this wave, we need to bring in everyone we can, that is, inclusion and be aware of the new dangers that this poses, that is, security.

sentences.text: I will speak on the topic of digital inclusion and Minister Josephine Teo will speak on issues related to digital trust and safety.

sections.summary: Jobs Transformation Maps, SkillsFuture, Workforce Singapore and IMDA's TeSA programme help workers prepare for tech-enabled roles and transit to tech jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Some examples include how we are using Jobs Transformation Maps (JTMs), which are specific to different sectors, help employers and workers understand and prepare themselves for future tech-enabled job roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: SkillsFuture and Workforce Singapore offer programmes to support workers to upskill and reskill to take on new jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: For those who wish to transit to tech roles, they can tap on IMDA's TechSkills Accelerator (TeSA) programme.

sections.label: Voucher claims by households

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Within a week of the launch, 80% of the 1.27 million Singaporean households have claimed their vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Last year, close to 400,000 transactions for services such as Singpass applications, CPF and IRAS services were completed at ServiceSG Centres.

sections.label: DigitalAccess@Home scheme support
sections.summary: IMDA introduced DigitalAccess@Home in April last year to support lower-income households with subsidised broadband and digital devices, supporting about 6,800 households since.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: IMDA introduced the DigitalAccess@Home scheme in April last year to support lower-income households with subsidised broadband and digital devices through a simplified and streamlined application process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Since then, we have supported about 6,800 households.
