sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Under this programme, SGQR has facilitated an average of 5.1 million transactions worth $42 million per month between June and November last year.

sections.label: Subtitles and assistive technology support
sections.summary: 61% of free-to-air TV programmes carry subtitles for deaf and hard-of-hearing audiences, with a 70% accessibility target by 2030 and MSF's Assistive Technology Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Today, 61% of free-to-air TV programmes carry subtitles for the deaf and hard-of-hearing audiences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We are working with Mediacorp to achieve our target of 70% coverage of free-to-air TV broadcasts accessible through sign language interpretation, captioning or subtitling by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Persons with disabilities who need assistive technology, such as a specialised keyboard and mouse, can tap on the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF)'s Assistive Technology Fund, which provides individuals with a means-tested subsidy of up to 90% of the cost of assistive technology devices, subject to a lifetime cap of $40,000.

sections.label: DfL partners and beneficiaries
sections.summary: Over 140 DfL partners have reached out to more than 270,000 beneficiaries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Over 140 DfL partners have reached out to more than 270,000 beneficiaries.

sections.label: Digital Skills for Life launch
sections.summary: IMDA will launch Digital Skills for Life (DSL) today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: To support this, IMDA will launch Digital Skills for Life (DSL) today.

sections.label: Seniors Go Digital feedback
sections.summary: Insights came from reaching over 280,000 seniors through Seniors Go Digital and from 16,000 pilot learners' feedback.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: But more importantly, we heard from Singaporeans themselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We learned from our insights from reaching out to more than 280,000 seniors through the Seniors Go Digital programme over the last three years and I would like to especially thank the 16,000 learners who were part of the pilot last year for their valuable feedback.

sections.label: Digital Skills for Life rollout
sections.summary: English digital resources roll out from this month, with Mandarin, Malay and Tamil resources by the first half of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The digital resources in English will be rolled out progressively from this month, and resources in Mandarin, Malay and Tamil will be available by the first half of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Digital Skills for Life (DSL) is a bottom-up movement, and we hope to see more partners and organisations join in, pooling our efforts to achieve success together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We will make the relevant content and other teaching materials available online for partners to use for free.

sections.label: Kinder online space heartware
sections.summary: Beyond hardware and software, Singapore must nurture heartware to foster a kinder, safer and more inclusive online space.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We have a strong "hardware" foundation in terms of access to devices and broadband connectivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We are strengthening our "software" layer by building up Singaporeans' skills and competencies to navigate the online space safely and confidently to fully benefit from exciting digital opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: However, as many Members have spoken passionately about, we must aspire to go beyond the "hardware" and "software", and nurture our "heartware" on how we treat one another and to foster a kinder online space for all where we make an effort to listen with the aim to understand, instead of shouting to press across our point; where we make an effort to respect another person's viewpoints and find common ground even if we disagree on certain issues; where we make an effort to offer a kind word, instead of joining in to spread negativity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We trust that there are norms which govern how we conduct ourselves and interact with one another.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We must aspire to bring this to the online space as well where our seniors will be able to go online safely without anxiety; where our children can go online confidently without having the fear of cyberbullying or encountering harmful online content.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Each one of us can play our part to build a safer, more inclusive and kinder digital society.

sentences.text: Of every $100 value-added in our economy, at least $17 can now be attributed to digital-related activities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: It amounted to $106 billion in 2022, more than financial services and insurance, and comparable with wholesale trade.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: There are, today, more than 200,000 tech jobs in Singapore, earning median wages that are higher than that of the resident workforce.

sections.label: SG Cyber Safe sector initiatives
sections.summary: In the next phase of the SG Cyber Safe Programme, CSA will introduce sector-specific cybersecurity initiatives starting with healthcare and manufacturing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In the next phase of the SG Cyber Safe Programme for enterprises, CSA will introduce sector-specific cybersecurity initiatives, starting with healthcare and manufacturing.

sections.label: AI governance and AI Verify
sections.summary: Before the 2019 National AI Strategy, Singapore introduced a Model AI Governance Framework, and in 2021 developed AI Verify.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Members may recall that even before we launched our first National AI Strategy or NAIS in 2019, we had introduced a Model AI Governance Framework or MGF – the first of its kind in the region.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In 2021, Singapore became one of the first in the world to develop a testing framework and software toolkit for safe and responsible AI, which we call AI Verify.

sections.label: AI bias and explainability
sections.summary: Mitigating bias and enhancing explainability of AI models are crucial, and MGF 2.0 is to be released for public consultation later this month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Mitigating biasness and enhancing the explainability of AI models are also crucial to developing and deploying them responsibly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We aim to release MGF 2.0 for public consultation later this month.

sections.label: ASCom froze bank accounts
sections.summary: In the first half of 2023, the ASCom froze over 9,000 bank accounts and recovered about $50.8 million of victims' losses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In the first half of 2023, the ASCom froze over 9,000 bank accounts and recovered about $50.8 million of the victims' losses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The volume of suspicious international calls blocked in 2023 has nearly doubled compared to a year ago.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To deal with this more effectively, we introduced the Online Criminal Harms Act (OCHA), which will be progressively implemented from this year.

sections.label: No further CPF scam losses
sections.summary: Since then, there have been no further losses to scams due to unauthorised CPF withdrawals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Since then, there have been no further losses to scams due to unauthorised CPF withdrawals.

sections.label: Shared Responsibility Framework accountability
sections.summary: The upcoming Shared Responsibility Framework will further enhance the accountability of banks and telcos in protecting customers from phishing scams.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Several MPs also spoke about the need for larger companies to take more responsibility to mitigate scams by unauthorised transactions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This year, the upcoming Shared Responsibility Framework (SRF) will further enhance the accountability of the banks and telcos in protecting their customers from the threat of phishing scams.

sections.label: Singapore anti-scam efforts praised
sections.summary: Singapore is regarded as a leader in fighting scams, with initiatives like call blocking, SMS Sender ID Registry, kill switches, Anti-Scam Command and ScamShield.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Agencies are, therefore, studying longer-term solutions, such as the Fast IDentity Online (FIDO) passkeys that were mentioned by Ms Tin.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Our efforts include exchanging information on the latest scam variants and strategies to combat scams.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: However, all of these efforts notwithstanding, this may still beg the question, "Has Singapore been slack in fighting scams?" On the contrary, Singapore is widely regarded as a leader in thought and action when it comes to battling scams.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: When interacting with our international counterparts, I can only share with you how much they marvel at some of the initiatives that we have put in place, which they consider quite unthinkable in their own context and still quite cutting edge.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: And these include widespread call blocking, the SMS Sender ID Registry (SSIR) and the kill switches that the banks now use; and also CPF Board.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The fact that we have an Anti-Scam Command, which involves the co-location of banks and, soon, other entities that we are speaking with; the fact that we have ScamShield; and something that people in the trade are very interested about: the backend processes that none of us will get to talk about in this room – among the agencies and all the stakeholders to smoothen the process of following up on leads – that is something that they find very difficult to even bring about.

sections.label: Safe App Standard for developers

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: As apps are the most common way to transact online, we also need app developers to design for security.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This is why Cyber Security Agency (CSA) is publishing a new recommended Safe App Standard (Standard) that app developers should adopt to ensure that high-risk monetary transactions performed on their apps are secure.

sections.label: Guidelines protecting vulnerable telco consumers
sections.summary: IMDA published Advisory Guidelines for telcos to protect vulnerable consumers from being tricked into signing up and paying for phone lines used for scams.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To strengthen safeguards against them being tricked into signing up and footing the bill for phone lines used for scams, IMDA has published the Advisory Guidelines for telcos to protect vulnerable consumers.

sections.label: Centre for Advanced Technologies in Online Safety
sections.summary: MCI and A*STAR will launch CATOS, a platform bringing together research partners, companies and practitioners to build capabilities for a safer Internet.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: As a first step, MCI and the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR) will officially launch the Centre for Advanced Technologies in Online Safety (CATOS).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Centre will be a platform to bring together our community of research partners, companies and practitioners in Singapore to build capabilities for a safer Internet.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Such capabilities may include tools and measures to: (a) detect harmful content, such as deepfakes and non-factual claims; (b) inject watermarks or trace the origin of digital content; and (c) empower vulnerable groups with resources to verify information they encounter online.

sections.label: Transaction Safety Ratings and Victim Care Officers
sections.summary: The E-commerce Marketplace Transaction Safety Ratings inform how secure platforms are against scams, and SPF trained volunteer Victim Care Officers to support victims.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We should use available tools to make more informed decisions when transacting online.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: These include the E-commerce Marketplace Transaction Safety Ratings (TSR), which provide information on how secure an e-commerce platform is against scams.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We understand the panic and anxiety that victims go through.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: That is why the SPF has trained volunteer Victim Care Officers to provide emotional and practical support to victims.

sections.label: SPF bank account freezes

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: SPF only freezes bank accounts when there is reason to suspect that they are involved in criminal activities.

sections.label: Victims applying to withdraw money

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Victims can also make an application to the Courts to withdraw money for reasonable living or other legitimate expenses.

sections.label: Three new anti-scam measures
sections.summary: The Government will introduce three measures: enhancing mobile application security, advisory guidelines for telcos, and developing advanced anti-scam technologies.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Government will introduce three new measures to further strengthen our defences against scams.

sentences.text: They are: enhancing the security of mobile applications; advisory guidelines for telcos to protect vulnerable consumers; and efforts to develop advanced technologies to combat scams.

sections.label: Seniors worried about scams

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First of all, according to the IMDA's Singapore Digital Society Report released in November, the statistics show that 99% of persons aged 60 and above are worried about becoming scam victims.

sections.label: New digital infrastructure task force
sections.summary: A new task force on Resilience and Security of Digital Infrastructure and Services is to oversee matters of public confidence.

sentences.text: Last of all, the fifth reason I would offer is that with the setting up of this new task force on Resilience and Security of Digital Infrastructure and Services, I believe that its purpose is to oversee matters of public confidence.

sections.label: Singapore measures against online harms
sections.summary: Singapore introduced the Codes of Practice for Online Safety and Content Code for Social Media Services in 2022 and passed the Online Criminal Harms Act in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In Singapore, we have taken active steps to mitigate the danger of online harms by introducing the Codes of Practice for Online Safety and the Content Code for Social Media Services in 2022 and also passing the Online Criminal Harms Act, as was referenced earlier in the debate, in 2023.

sections.label: Online harms topology and victim reporting
sections.summary: A World Economic Forum topology breaks down online harms, and victims are unwilling to seek remediation for reasons including anonymity and ineffectual reporting channels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The World Economic Forum has recently developed a Topology of Online Harms that had provided a more nuanced breakdown of such harms, examining them from content production, distribution, consumption and whether such harms took place through interactions with others – contact-based – or were through behaviours facilitated by technology, which is more based on conduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What is worrisome is the unwillingness of victims to seek remediation with the top three reasons being: (a) the belief that perpetrators will not be brought to justice due to anonymity of the Internet; (b) ineffectual reporting channels of social media platforms; and (c) victims not knowing what to do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Separately, in a report titled "10 Online Harm Myths" published by SG Her Empowerment, women between the age of 25 and 34 are more likely to suffer from online harms and a good portion of youths believe that online harms are less serious than offline ones and would stop once you go offline.

sections.label: Mandatory online learning modules
sections.summary: MOE is encouraged to create mandatory online learning modules on online harms, their effects on victims, and where to seek help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: First, I would like to encourage MOE to create mandatory online learning modules for students to better understand the wrongful content nature of online harms, how their distribution and consumption will cause distress and hurt to victims and where to seek help if they are victims.

sections.label: Banning offending IP addresses

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: When social media platforms take down identified offensive online content, can they consider banning or restricting the offending IP address from accessing their platforms or from creating new social media accounts?

sections.label: Annual online harm report
sections.summary: It asks whether the Government will work with social media platforms to compile an annual report on online harm cases and actions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To further encourage victims of online harms to seek for help and to increase their confidence that actions will be taken against perpetrators, would the Government then consider with working even with social media platforms to compile an annual report of the number of online harm cases reported, the number of successful actions taken, the type of actions taken against the perpetrators and the number of convictions made in a year?

sections.label: POFMA passed in 2019

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: When the Protection from Online Falsehoods and Manipulation Act was passed in 2019, we were one of the first countries in the world to pass a law tackling online falsehoods.

sections.label: SimplyGo feedback and digital inclusivity
sections.summary: It asks how the Minister will respond to digital inclusivity and negative SimplyGo feedback, and notes PAP MPs' 13 calls to action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In view that, I would like to ask the Minister how she will respond in relation to what we have discussed and debated today about digital inclusivity, how she will respond to the many negative feedback from Singaporeans about SimplyGo.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Incidents like SimplyGo will affect the trust in digital systems in the long run.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Our PAP MPs, Ms Jessica Tan, Mr Sharael Taha, Ms Hany Soh, Ms Nadia Samdin, Dr Wan Rizal, Mr Yip Hon Weng, Ms Mariam Jaafar, Mr Vikram Nair and Mr Darryl David have put forth a total of 13 calls to action, many more, if we double click into these calls of action, calling on our Government, industry players and individuals, like you and me, to play a more proactive role in ensuring a safe and inclusive online environment as Singapore continues to forge ahead into the digital future.

sections.label: Government digital safeguards assurance
sections.summary: It states the Government has put in place initiatives and safeguards including tools, codes, legislation, financial assistance and support schemes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: That being the case, having heard from Minister Josephine Teo and Senior Minister of State Tan Kiat How earlier, I believe we can feel more assured now, with the many initiatives and safeguards that the Government has already put in place to protect and enable our citizens in the digital economy and digital society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: These include pooling of resources and expertise, tools, codes and legislation to tackle scams, harmful online content, misinformation and data protection, as well as financial assistance and support schemes to enable digital access and empower the vulnerable.

sections.label: Singapore proactive on digital challenges
sections.summary: Singapore has been proactive in tackling digital challenges, unlike some advanced countries, and the Government is open to 13 calls to action.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: So, instead of claiming that there is a "crisis of confidence" in Singapore towards digital, it is more appropriate to note that Singapore has been proactive in tackling the challenges, when some advanced countries actually found it unthinkable to do.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: I am also especially appreciative that the Government has been open to our 13 calls to action and committed to taking actions on our calls made.

sections.label: Balancing digital risk and innovation
sections.summary: Risks and harms should be managed with rigour without adding disproportionate friction to digital transactions or meaningful innovations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: While we want rigour in how we manage risks and prevent harms to our people, we also want to ensure that we do not add disproportionate amount of friction to digital transactions or meaningful innovations.
